name: @zebra-design-system/patterns
note: Generated when the patterns are packaged. Do not edit: change the .md files and package again.

patterns.title: Screen composition
patterns.summary: Where each part of a screen goes, how it relates to what's around it, and how it changes with the size of the screen. These principles describe roles (a filter, a system notification, a primary action), not a particular component, so they hold in any product and any design system. If a product doesn't have a role, the principles for it don't apply.

patterns.title: Navigation and flow
patterns.summary: How people move between places and through steps: structure, global and local navigation, back and exit, deep links, wizards, question flows, task loops, interruption, handoff, onboarding and sign-in.
sections: Deep links, notifications and return paths
Structure across roles, tenants and devices

patterns.title: Controls and interaction
patterns.summary: How each control responds when it's used: buttons, links, choices, text and number entry, dates, selection, menus, gestures, keys, saving, undo, inline editing, scanning, hardware input and the motion tied to all of these.
sections: Switches, checkboxes, radios and segmented controls
Motion and haptics tied to interaction

patterns.title: States, feedback and recovery
patterns.summary: What happens in each state, and how messages behave over time: loading, empty, error, success, offline, sync, permissions, sessions, device states, message lifetime and severity.

patterns.title: Sizes and devices
patterns.summary: What changes with the space available, the input used and the kind of device: size classes, grids, how each kind of component changes, overflow, text growth and translation, orientation, density, pinned regions and the keyboard, safe areas, form factors, input modes and viewing conditions. Widths and margins are relationships here; the host system supplies the values.

patterns.title: Accessibility
patterns.summary: The floors every other principle sits on, and how the interface behaves for screen readers, keyboards, switch and voice control, magnification, and people working in hard conditions. These principles come before every other principle. Ratios and sizes below are minimums, not design values. The system's tokens supply the values, and every value must clear these floors in every theme.

patterns.title: Content and copy
patterns.summary: What the interface says: voice, labels, messages, terms, and how numbers, dates and plurals are written.

patterns.title: Visual foundations and theming
patterns.summary: The look, stated as roles and relationships: colour, states, themes, type, weight, space, shape, elevation, icons, imagery, motion as look, brand, and re-theming one system to a given product. Values come from the host system's tokens. These principles say what each role means, how roles relate, and what may and may not change when a product re-themes. Every principle here must clear the contrast floors in every theme.
sections: Colour for urgent and device states
True content, scripts and Zebra hardware

patterns.title: AI in the interface
patterns.summary: How AI behaves inside the product: where it's offered, how its suggestions are accepted and undone, how its output is marked and sourced, how sure it says it is, how it acts on someone's behalf, how it waits, fails, learns, remembers, listens and sees, and how it hands over. The aim throughout is the right amount of reliance, not the most trust.
sections: Confidence and checking what was meant

patterns.title: Data display
patterns.summary: How data is shown inside a collection, a record or a chart: choosing the form, table anatomy, list items, key–value records, status in data, numbers in data, cells, charts, live data, comparisons and maps.

references.title: Zebra devices
references.summary: The Zebra device families that run product UI. [05-sizes-devices.md](05-sizes-devices.md) says how to design for each form factor.

references.title: Terms
references.summary: What each pattern word means, in one place. Each rule file also defines the terms it uses at its top; where the two differ, the rule file is right. Rule files use these words and nothing more specific, so the rules apply to any component system. [zebra.md](zebra.md) maps each word onto the Zebra Design System's components and tokens.

references.title: Zebra binding
references.summary: Maps each pattern word in [terms.md](terms.md) onto the Zebra Design System. Read it with the pattern files when the project is built with a Zebra library. A project on another system does not need this file.

recipes.title: Act on one object
recipes.summary: A screen about one thing: what it is, how it is doing, and what can be done to it.

recipes.title: Capture
recipes.summary: Taking something in from the world: a scan, a photo, a reading.

recipes.title: Converse
recipes.summary: Asking in words and getting an answer, with a person or an AI assistant.

recipes.title: Create in steps
recipes.summary: Making something new, one step at a time, ending in a review.

recipes.title: Find one item
recipes.summary: A collection the person searches, filters and scans to reach the one item they came for.

recipes.title: Monitor
recipes.summary: A screen that shows whether things are all right, and what isn't.

recipes.title: Work through many
recipes.summary: A run of items handled one after another, the same way each time.
